digest.component_or_area: plan-review severity grading and impact model
propositions: The 'undecomposed' axis fires on only 0.107% of plan-v3 verified findings (11/10,250) and 0.153% of plan-v4 findings (18/11,773), two orders of magnitude below other severity axes, yet holds full hard-override power (floors impact to 0.85)

The cited deterministic suppressor (G5 veto) that allegedly explains the low fire rate fired zero times across 2,000 recorded reviews and is inapplicable to 90%+ of the reviewed population (which is childless)

The inverse population of findings whose text matches flat/undecomposed patterns but scored axis-grade 'none' consists primarily of regex false positives on code/module decomposition, not missed defects
The hard-override floor of 0.85 is miscalibrated: 25 of 29 fires have no other hard-override criterion, and 16 fires are graded 'low' which should not floor impact identically to 'high' grades
The axis text incorrectly cites an inert suppressor mechanism as justification for conservative grading, and requires prompt rewrites across multiple reviewer documents to remove this false rationale
